properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 13 at 1:24PM PST until November 13 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
SVREKA

The National Weather Service in Eureka has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
North Central Humboldt County in northwestern California...

* Until 200 PM PST.

* At 124 PM PST, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles north of
Trinidad, or 11 miles southwest of Orick, moving northeast at 15
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Big Lagoon
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.
properties.area: Humboldt, CA

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 13 at 1:18PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:

miles north of Trinidad, or 11 miles southwest of Orick, moving
northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 30 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Big Lagoon
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.
properties.area: Northern Coastal Humboldt; Northeastern Interior Humboldt

properties.description:

Whitehorn, or 6 miles northeast of Shelter Cove, moving northeast at
10 mph.

HAZARD...Landspouts, wind gusts up to 30 mph, and half inch size
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 1:53PM CST until November 14 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern
Illinois...
Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may be clogged with debris, increasing the risk of
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 153 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain has fallen since Thursday
evening. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the
Turkey Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above
bankfull.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Far East side of Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City,
Merrillville, South Shore, East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart,
Lansing, Crown Point, Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith,
Dyer, South Deering, St. John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of
the Four Seasons, Whiting, Winfield and New Chicago.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor
drainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in
the advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.
properties.area: Cook, IL; Lake, IN

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 10:51AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just at Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain
steady around Minor Flood Stage into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 5.5 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1130 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 9:40AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 937 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 2:15 PM
Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri
11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun
11/15.
* West Sacramento: 1.2 ft above normal (5.5 ft MLLW) at 5:28
PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM
Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun
11/15.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12,
+7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/14.
- These predictions include up to +1.1 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary up to an hour throughout the San
Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
properties.area: Solano, CA
